articles.title: NBA 2K25 Is Getting Delisted After Just 2 Years, and Single Player Story Mode Will Become Unplayable
articles.summary: NBA 2K25 is being delisted after just two years, and players will soon no longer be able to play the game's single player story mode.
articles.body:
NBA 2K25 is being delisted after just two years, and players will soon no longer be able to play the game's single player story mode.

Launched back in September 2024, NBA 2K25 is the latest NBA game that is being pulled from digital stores. 2K will be pulling the game from purchase starting on October 30, 2026. Additionally, online servers will be shut down on January 1, 2027. As a result, the game's multiplayer modes and MyCareer, the game's single-player story mode, will become unplayable. MyCareer is linked to the game's online capabilities, as progression and the game's virtual currency are all dependent on a connection to the servers. If there are no servers, the mode becomes unplayable.

Those who purchase NBA 2K25 before October 30 will be able to freely download the game and play offline modes whenever they want. You can read 2K's statement on the matter below.

"As of January 1, 2027, you'll no longer be able to play multiplayer games or access any online game modes. MyCAREER and MyTEAM will no longer be available, and it will no longer be possible to earn Virtual Currency (VC). While you will still be able to enjoy Play Now, MyNBA, The W, and MyWNBA, any features that require a connection to 2K servers will be unavailable. This includes multiplayer, Online Leagues, and community sharing."

Although it's not uncommon for much older games to have their servers shut down, 2K has been delisting and killing recent NBA games in the last few years. While there's likely a very small percentage of players playing these titles anyway since the player base often moves to the current game, it is a disappointing move. It forces players to move to the new games, regardless if they want to or not. Although most sports games have modest iterations with each new entry, some titles remove features and modes, meaning some legacy content is outright non-existent anymore.

If you were a fan of NBA 2K's standalone All-Star Team-Up mode, that is no longer accessible because previous versions of the game were delisted and taken offline. It also means a lot of your effort in MyCareer is rendered somewhat useless since it has an expiration date. However, given fans keep buying the series, it doesn't seem to be hurting the franchise.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Una estrella de la Euroliga, multada tras dar positivo en un control de alcoholemia
articles.standfirst: Carsen Edwards, escolta del Zalgiris, fue detenido durante un control rutinario por conducir en estado de embriaguez
articles.summary: Carsen Edwards, escolta del Zalgiris, fue detenido durante un control rutinario por conducir en estado de embriaguez
articles.body: El Zalgiris Kaunas multó este lunes a su jugador Carsen Edwards después de que fuese detenido en Lituania por conducir su vehículo en estado de embriaguez, según informó el propio club. Pese a que no ha dado más detallas sobre la sanción ni el positivo del escolta estadounidense, el portal lituano Krepsinis.net indicó que la tasa de alcoholemia de Edwards fue de 1,07%. El incidente se produjo durante un control policial rutinario en la noche del domingo, tan solo unas horas después de que el Zalgiris venciese al Lietkabelis en su encuentro de la liga lituana. "El Kaunas Zalgiris ha evaluado la situación del jugador Carsen Edwards, quien fue detenido al volante de un vehículo en estado de embriaguez. El club ha investigado las circunstancias del incidente y, de acuerdo con el reglamento del equipo, ha decidido imponerle una multa", dijo el club en su web. El club señaló que Edwards reconoció su error, asumió la responsabilidad de sus actos y mostró su "sincero arrepentimiento tras lo ocurrido". "El jugador comprende la gravedad de la falta cometida, reconoce que su comportamiento no estuvo a la altura de los valores del club ni de los estándares profesionales que se esperan de él, y lo lamenta profundamente", indicó. El escolta llegó este verano al Zalgiris después de su gran temporada en el Virtus Bolonia italiano. Reconocido por su capacidad para anotar, Edwards promedia esta campaña 16 puntos, 2 asistencias, un rebote y 10,3 de valoración por partido en la Euroliga. El conjunto lituano será el próximo rival del Barça en la máxima competición europea, este viernes en el Palau Blaugrana de Barcelona.

images.caption: Carsen Edwards, durante un encuentro del Zalgiris Kaunas.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns on chances of signing extension with Knicks before season: 'It don't look good'
articles.summary: The All-Star big man continues to sound pessimistic about his odds of signing a new deal before the start of the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
As the New York Knicks prepare to begin their NBA title defense with a preseason opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday night, star big man Karl-Anthony Towns reiterated his frustration over stalled negotiations on a contract extension to remain with the Knicks for years to come.

"Simply put, I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said Monday before the preseason opener. "And none of those things are close to happening." Asked about the possibility of an agreement before the regular season starts, Towns said, "It don't look good."

"Simply put, I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said Monday before the preseason opener. "And none of those things are close to happening."

Asked about the possibility of an agreement before the regular season starts, Towns said, "It don't look good."

Towns, who played perhaps the best basketball of his life during New York's run to a title back in June, has one fully guaranteed season left on his contract, and holds a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign. He is eligible for an extension worth a maximum of $276 million over four years — a deal with an average annual value of $69 million per season, which would make him one of the highest-paid players in the league .

The Knicks have thus far balked at that price tag, according to multiple reports . Their reluctance owes partly to the prospective perils of paying a 7-footer north of $70 million as he enters his mid-30s, but primarily to the painful financial crunch of paying to keep together a championship roster — a difficult fiscal reality that makes Towns' extension negotiation one of the most interesting to monitor in the league heading into the 2026-27 season.

As it stands, New York has just under $226.7 million in salary committed on the books for the 2027-28 season, according to Spotrac — about $9.3 million below the projected second apron line for that season. That figure includes team options on Josh Hart (who is also currently eligible for, and very much interested in, a contract extension ) and 2024 draftees Pacôme Dadiet and Tyler Kolek; it does not include a new deal for sixth man Miles "Deuce" McBride, who has dramatically outperformed his three-year, $13 million contract and is also eligible for, and very much interested in, a contract extension .

The second apron line is critical because, a scant four days after the Knicks finished off their five-game victory over the San Antonio Spurs , owner James L. Dolan went on New York radio station WFAN and made it clear that he did not intend to approve an offseason spending plan that would increase the team's total salary commitments for this season past that second apron threshold.

Dolan called the prospect of spending into the second apron something "that you'd have to be, you know, suicidal to do." Crossing that line not only imposes a higher tax rate on high-spending teams, but also strips away team-building and roster-management tools like access to salary-cap exceptions, the ability to aggregate players' salaries in trades, the option of sending cash to another team to grease the skids on a swap, and the freedom to acquire players in sign-and-trade deals, among other restrictions.

Dolan's radio-appearance edict reportedly "blindsided" the Knicks front office, which wanted to go over the second apron after patiently and meticulously building a championship roster . Instead, New York spent its summer maneuvering to stay below that $222 million line — and, in the process, lost backup center Mitchell Robinson , who signed a three-year, $47.4 million deal with the Boston Celtics .

It's unclear whether Dolan's "stay below the second apron" mandate will apply beyond this season. If it does, though, it becomes exceedingly difficult to envision a scenario in which the Knicks — who will also see Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby become extension-eligible next summer — keep the core that just won the championship together. The math essentially demands significant financial sacrifice, beyond even the cost savings that New York was able to realize when Brunson opted to extend a year ahead of free agency and when Anunoby and Mikal Bridges took slightly less than their maximum salaries in their respective re-ups.

Towns has publicly and privately expressed a willingness to make that sort of sacrifice. The issue, of course, is just how big a sacrifice a six-time All-Star and three-time All-NBA selection who just performed at his best on the biggest stage imaginable should be expected to make.

The Knicks have reportedly offered Towns a four-year, $200 million extension — less than he got from the Timberwolves in 2022 , and more than $75 million below his max. Towns, very clearly, does not feel that offer accurately reflects the contributions he's made since arriving before the start of the 2024-25 season — a span in which he's averaged 22.2 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game on 51/40/84 shooting splits, made a pair of All-Star teams and one All-NBA team, helped the Knicks reach the conference finals for the first time in a quarter-century, and then helped them hoist the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy for the first time in 53 years.

Asked on Monday whether he felt he deserved to be rewarded for that level of achievement on his next deal, Towns told reporters : "No s***, Sherlock. I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys think I have something else to prove."

Towns evidently believes he's proven more than enough to merit an offer significantly above the ones New York have presented thus far — offers aimed at affording Knicks team president Leon Rose and his front office enough flexibility to try to get Brunson, Anunoby and Hart (and potentially McBride, though the math appears very tight ) extended, all while remaining under the second apron in 2028-29 and potentially beyond.

As displeased as Towns might be by the state of his negotiations, he's still under contract and set to make $57.1 million this season. The Knicks still have the opportunity to extend him at any point during the regular season — though, as Fred Katz of The Athletic recently noted , doing it before the year would allow them to extend Towns off his 2027-28 player option, unlocking potentially advantageous structures as they prepare for a major leap in Brunson's salary on his next deal.

It's also worth noting that the Knicks don't have to stay below the second apron; the league's rules don't dictate that they must, or anything. They are, as SNY's Ian Begley put it , "voluntarily limited" by Dolan's public and apparently ongoing insistence that he will not authorize spending above that line. If the owner changes his tune on that, then the tenor of Towns' negotiation — and Hart's, and McBride's, and so on — would likely change, too.

It doesn't seem like such a change is forthcoming, though. That has Towns (and Hart, and McBride, and so on) pessimistic about the prospect of getting a deal done before the start of the season, and preparing to head into a new campaign with an unwelcome uncertainty hanging over his head.

"In my experience," Towns said, according to James L. Edwards III of The Athletic , "you just approach the moments right now, and let it go where it goes."

articles.title: Big dreams: Suns hope young bigs can help team take next step
articles.summary: PHOENIX – Dillon Brooks has high hopes for Koa Peat. That is, if Peat can move past an issue common with rookies. “He’s a little shy,” Brooks said, “so I...
articles.body:
PHOENIX – Dillon Brooks has high hopes for Koa Peat . That is, if Peat can move past an issue common with rookies.

"He's a little shy," Brooks said, "so I got to break that wall."

Peat is one of at least four young bigs whom the Suns veterans hope will break down walls and earn significant playing time this season. That has been a key theme for the team as it begins the preseason on Monday in Detroit.

The Suns finished 45-37 last season, earning an eighth-place finish in the Western Conference. After advancing past the play-in round, Oklahoma City swept them. Still, it was a major improvement from the previous season when Phoenix finished 10 games below .500 and missed the playoffs.

With the help of some veterans, the Suns are hoping to build on last season's success by getting big contributions from their last two top draft picks and a crop of young bigs.

Heading into the preseason, Suns veterans have spoken highly of second-year center Khaman Maluach, who was the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NBA draft, second-year forward Rasheer Fleming and rookie forward Koa Peat, who won four state championships at Gilbert Perry High and helped Arizona to a Final Four before the Suns selected him 30th overall in the 2026 NBA draft.

The Suns obtained the draft rights to Maluach as part of the trade that sent Kevin Durant to Houston. Fleming, who was originally drafted by Minnesota, was also part of that seven-team blockbuster.

Maluach saw few minutes on the court during his rookie year, appearing in 46 games and starting only once. Fleming also started just one game and played in 55 as a rookie. But Maluach made big strides in the offseason, and the big man's prospects look different this season.

Maluach averaged 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds and had two blocks in the 2026 NBA Summer League, leading the league in rebounds averaged and earning second-team All-NBA Summer League honors.

Then came the news that center Mark Williams, whom the Suns had just re-signed and was the likely starter, would miss an indefinite amount of time after shoulder surgery.

"I pray for Mark," Maluach said. "That's my teammate. It's an opportunity for me to step up, but I'm here to do whatever it takes, what the team needs. That's how I see it and I'm going to do whatever it takes for us to be in a good spot."

Williams' absence gives Maluach a chance to break into the rotation and possibly the starting lineup, but he'll be competing with former Phoenix Desert Vista High star Oso Ighodaro for the starting center spot. Ighodaro is entering his third year in the league.

"It puts more (pressure) on Oso and Man-Man (Maluach)," Suns coach Jordan Ott said. "These two guys are ultra-competitive, ultra-young. They understand that they have to play with a certain type of physicality. These two centers battle it every day."

Despite the competition, Ighodaro said it's all love between the players and that helps them push each other to be better.

"I love playing with him," Ighodaro said. "Even in pickup when we'll be on opposite teams, we'll be talking to each other, helping each other, giving each other pointers. I feel like we both have a similar mindset in terms of the process and getting better. I'm grateful to have him as my teammate."

During the offseason, Maluach reached out to Suns star Devin Booker and asked to work out with him to build a better connection.

"He has done this for a long time," Maluach said. "He has a lot of tools or a lot of stuff that I can learn from him. As a young center, just being able to go to him and being able to ask him what I should do. He's kind of like a coach himself and I get to learn a lot from him."

Maluach isn't the only player learning from vets. Peat, who averaged 14.1 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists during his only season at Arizona, has benefitted as well. The Suns pulled some strings during the draft to obtain him, sending the 47th pick in 2026, two future second-round picks and cash considerations to the New York Knicks for the 30th pick.

"We had Koa much higher in our rankings," Suns general manager Brian Gregory said. "As the night progressed and it looked like there might be an opportunity for us to pull a couple of levers to be in position, the excitement grew and grew. Everywhere he's been, all he's done is win."

Ighodaro isn't surprised the Suns pursued his fellow Valley local.

"He doesn't carry himself like a rookie," Ighodaro said. "He wants to learn. He wants to get better. He's an extremely good rebounder. He guards the ball defensively. If he continues to do so, he'll impact winning."

Suns guard Jalen Green said the veterans will shepherd Peat.

"He's going to learn a lot from everybody on the team," Green said. "Especially like Booker, Miles (Bridges). He's got that bump. He's playing mid-range. He's got a mid-range shot. Can't ask for nothing else, and just learning the whole summer."

Fleming is another player hoping to break into the rotation.

"He continues to raise the floor by his work, his care and his understanding of who he is as a player," Ott said of Fleming. "He has no idea where his ceiling is, nor do we. He has physical gifts that you cannot teach."

Green also took note of Fleming's work ethic.

"That's who he is as a player," Green said. "I don't see anything else but him continuing to do that. I'll see him be in the gym in the morning and come back at night. He loves the work and he's putting that time in."

Booker said the young players as a whole have displayed a work ethic and attention to detail that will serve them and the team well.

"They're always the first in the gym," Booker said. "They bring their youth and energy every day. They're getting extra shots up. They all ask the right questions. I haven't seen a bad rookie or a bad young fella in a while now."

articles.title: Kansas State ends Jerome Tang dispute with a $12M settlement after firing
articles.summary: MANHATTAN, Kansas (AP) — Kansas State has reached a settlement with former basketball coach Jerome Tang that includes a $12 million payment.The athletic depa...
articles.body:
MANHATTAN, Kansas (AP) — Kansas State has reached a settlement with former basketball coach Jerome Tang that includes a $12 million payment.

The athletic department and Tang announced the agreement Monday, ending a dispute that arose after the former Wildcats coach was fired for cause in February, threatening to void an $18.7 million buyout.

"This settlement allows both parties to move forward on agreed terms," Kansas State athletic director Gene Taylor said in a statement. "We're grateful for his contributions to Kansas State basketball, including a memorable first season, and we wish him and his family well."

Kansas State announced it was firing Tang on Feb. 15, four days after a 29-point loss to Cincinnati.

After the game, a despondent Tang said that his players "do not deserve to wear this uniform" and that "there will be very few of them in it next year." The sound bite quickly made headlines, and the school ultimately fired Tang for cause, saying that he had embarrassed the school.

Tang told ESPN at the time that he disagreed with the "characterization of my termination." He also disputed the "for cause" nature of his dismissal.

In four seasons at Kansas State, the 59-year-old Tang was 71-57 overall and 29-39 in the Big 12. He led the Wildcats to a 26-10 mark and the Elite Eight, becoming the first head coach in program history to receive the Naismith Men's Basketball Coach of the Year Award.

In June, Tang rejoined Baylor coach Scott Drew's staff as associate head coach. Tang was on Drew's staff the first 19 seasons before going to Kansas State.
